blocks.p: *See-through* sets how much of the scene shows through the windows. It runs from 100, where a window is solid, down to 60, in steps of 10, and 90 is the default. It is set in *ZeD setup*, and from the window menu under *See-through*.

In the same list is *Solid while in use*. With it on, the window you are using is drawn solid while the other windows keep the see-through setting. A window is in use while the pointer is over it or the controller is in it; when the pointer or the controller leaves, the window goes back to the setting. Figure 16-1 shows the *Character* window in use by the controller at see-through 60.

caption: Figure 16-1
See-through 60 with Solid while in use on: the Character window, in use, stays solid.

marks.text: Solid while in use makes the window in use solid: here the controller is in the Character window.

blocks.p: Figure 16-2 shows the same *World* window at see-through 100 and at 60. Words, lines, pictures and controls stay solid at every setting; only the surface of the window lets the scene through.

caption: Figure 16-2
The World window at see-through 100, left, and 60, right.

marks.text: At 60 the scene behind, here the lot and a car, shows through the window.
